# UML3 to SQL DDL

<!-- GENERATED by tools/check_languages.py from traceability/uml3-to-languages.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Can a UML3 model be turned into a schema, and can an existing schema be read back into one? Each row is something SQL DDL expresses, how the major dialects spell it, and which UML3 construct carries it. UML3Data already models the logical and physical sides and the #mapsTo link between them, so the interesting rows are the physical details a CREATE statement needs and a class diagram traditionally drops.

## Coverage legend

* **COVERED**: a UML3 construct expresses it; the construct is named in the UML3 column
* **PARTIAL**: expressible, but with loss - the note says what is lost
* **GAP**: no UML3 construct expresses it; a requirement is needed if it matters
* **TBD**: not yet analyzed, or the dialect's behaviour has not been confirmed

## Targets

| Target | Version | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| ISO SQL | 9075:2023 | none; analysis only |
| PostgreSQL | 17 | none; analysis only |
| MySQL | 8.4 | none; analysis only |
| SQL Server | 2022 | none; analysis only |
| Oracle | 23ai | none; analysis only |

Dialect columns are written against PostgreSQL 17, MySQL 8.4, Microsoft SQL Server 2022 and Oracle 23ai, and against ISO/IEC 9075:2023 where the standard settles it. No database engine is installed on this machine, so unlike the Java and Rust columns of the language map nothing here has been executed; rows whose answer depends on engine behaviour are marked TBD.

## Schema objects

| Concept | Coverage | UML3 | ISO SQL | PostgreSQL | MySQL | SQL Server | Oracle | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Database / catalog | **COVERED** | `UML3Data::database` | CREATE DATABASE | CREATE DATABASE | CREATE DATABASE | CREATE DATABASE | pluggable database | — |
| Schema / namespace inside a database | **PARTIAL** | `SysML package` | CREATE SCHEMA | CREATE SCHEMA | schema = database | CREATE SCHEMA | schema = user | A package groups tables, but nothing says that the package IS a SQL schema, so a generator has to assume the convention. MySQL and Oracle conflate schema with database and user respectively, which a model should be able to state. |
| Table | **COVERED** | `UML3Data::table` | CREATE TABLE | CREATE TABLE | CREATE TABLE | CREATE TABLE | CREATE TABLE | — |
| Column | **COVERED** | `UML3Data::column` | column definition | column | column | column | column | — |
| View | **COVERED** | `UML3Data::dbView` | CREATE VIEW | CREATE VIEW | CREATE VIEW | CREATE VIEW | CREATE VIEW | The view exists as an element; the SELECT that defines it is the gap below. |
| The query behind a view | **GAP** | — | AS SELECT ... | AS SELECT | AS SELECT | AS SELECT | AS SELECT | A view without its query cannot be created. KerML has expressions, so a calculation could carry it, but nothing designates one as a view's defining query. |
| Materialized view | **GAP** | — | - | CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW | - | indexed view | materialized view | Not distinguishable from a plain view, and the refresh policy has nowhere to live. |

## Constraints

| Concept | Coverage | UML3 | ISO SQL | PostgreSQL | MySQL | SQL Server | Oracle | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primary key | **COVERED** | `UML3Data::primaryKey` | PRIMARY KEY | PRIMARY KEY | PRIMARY KEY | PRIMARY KEY | PRIMARY KEY | Composite keys are several #primaryKey columns on one table. |
| Foreign key | **COVERED** | `UML3Data::foreignKey` | REFERENCES | REFERENCES | REFERENCES | REFERENCES | REFERENCES | — |
| Referential action on delete or update | **GAP** | — | ON DELETE CASCADE | ON DELETE/UPDATE | ON DELETE/UPDATE | ON DELETE/UPDATE | ON DELETE only | Composition implies that a part dies with its whole, which is the intent behind CASCADE, but the model cannot state RESTRICT, SET NULL or NO ACTION, and Oracle supports no ON UPDATE at all. |
| Unique constraint | **COVERED** | `UML3Data::unique` | UNIQUE | UNIQUE | UNIQUE | UNIQUE | UNIQUE | — |
| NOT NULL | **COVERED** | `KerML multiplicity [1] against [0..1]` | NOT NULL | NOT NULL | NOT NULL | NOT NULL | NOT NULL | Multiplicity carries nullability; no keyword needed. |
| CHECK constraint | **PARTIAL** | `SysML constraint / assert constraint` | CHECK | CHECK | CHECK | CHECK | CHECK | A SysML constraint states the predicate, but nothing marks it as one the database should enforce rather than a tool, and the expression would have to be translated to SQL. |
| DEFAULT value | **COVERED** | `SysML feature value (= expression)` | DEFAULT | DEFAULT | DEFAULT | DEFAULT | DEFAULT | A default in the model is a feature value; a server-side default such as now() is an expression the generator must map. |

## Types

| Concept | Coverage | UML3 | ISO SQL | PostgreSQL | MySQL | SQL Server | Oracle | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sized numeric and string types | **COVERED** | `UML3Types::Facets` | NUMERIC(p,s), VARCHAR(n) | numeric, varchar | DECIMAL, VARCHAR | decimal, nvarchar | NUMBER, VARCHAR2 | @Facets carries precision, scale and length, which is exactly what a column needs. |
| Identity / auto-increment / sequence | **GAP** | — | GENERATED AS IDENTITY | identity / serial | AUTO_INCREMENT | IDENTITY | identity / sequence | #id says a column identifies the row, not that the database generates its value. Almost every real schema has one. |
| Date, time and time zone | **TBD** | — | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | timestamptz | DATETIME/TIMESTAMP | datetimeoffset | TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE | The SysML standard library has time and duration types; whether UML3Types gives a column-level mapping with time-zone semantics has not been checked. |
| JSON column | **GAP** | — | JSON | jsonb | JSON | json / nvarchar | JSON | A column whose value is a document has no UML3 form, although UML3Messaging can describe the document's shape - the two are not linked. |
| Enumerated column | **PARTIAL** | `SysML enum def` | CHECK constraint | CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM | ENUM | CHECK | CHECK | The enumeration exists in the model; which of the four physical encodings a dialect should use is not stated. |
| Array or collection column | **TBD** | — | ARRAY | type[] | - | - | nested table | A multi-valued attribute normally becomes a child table; when the dialect has arrays the choice is not expressible. |

| Concept | Coverage | UML3 | ISO SQL | PostgreSQL | MySQL | SQL Server | Oracle | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Trigger | **GAP** | — | CREATE TRIGGER | CREATE TRIGGER | CREATE TRIGGER | CREATE TRIGGER | CREATE TRIGGER | SysML has actions and state transitions, so the behaviour is modelable, but nothing binds one to a table event. |
| Stored procedure or function | **PARTIAL** | `UML3Core::operation` | CREATE PROCEDURE | CREATE FUNCTION | CREATE PROCEDURE | CREATE PROC | CREATE PROCEDURE | The signature is expressible as an operation; nothing says it lives in the database rather than the application, and the body is not modeled. |

## Mapping

| Concept | Coverage | UML3 | ISO SQL | PostgreSQL | MySQL | SQL Server | Oracle | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Logical entity mapped to a physical table | **COVERED** | `UML3Data::entity`, `UML3Data::mapsTo` | - | - | - | - | - | This is UML3's own contribution rather than a DDL feature: #mapsTo records which logical entity a table realizes, which is what makes a schema traceable to a domain model. |
| Association resolved to a foreign key or join table | **PARTIAL** | `UML3Core::association`, `UML3Data::relationship` | FK or junction table | same | same | same | same | Both the association and the resulting keys can be modeled, but the rule that a many-to-many becomes a junction table is left to the generator rather than stated. |

## Operations

| Concept | Coverage | UML3 | ISO SQL | PostgreSQL | MySQL | SQL Server | Oracle | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Schema migration / ALTER | **GAP** | — | ALTER TABLE | ALTER TABLE | ALTER TABLE | ALTER TABLE | ALTER TABLE | A model states the schema now; a migration is the difference between two versions of it. Nothing expresses a version or an upgrade path, and real databases are changed by migration, not by re-creation. |
| Grants, roles and row-level security | **GAP** | `UML3Data::Sensitivity` | GRANT | GRANT, RLS policy | GRANT | GRANT, RLS | GRANT, VPD | Sensitivity marks data that needs care, which is the classification half; who may read or write it is not expressible. |
| Column excluded from persistence | **COVERED** | `UML3Data::transient` | - | - | - | - | - | #transient marks an attribute the schema must not carry, which a generator needs in order to skip it. |
| Audit columns | **COVERED** | `UML3Data::audited` | - | trigger or extension | trigger | temporal table | flashback | #audited states the intent; which mechanism a dialect uses is a generator decision, and SQL Server temporal tables and Oracle flashback are not equivalent. |
